profile.headline: Software Engineer at Applied Invention
profile.summary:
I am a software engineer at Applied Invention in Cambridge, MA, where I work on a team developing an open source standard for Zero-trust Packet Routing (ZPR), a new approach to network and data security.

I hold a B.S. in Computer Science and Religion from Tufts University.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Skills: Linux · Git · Lua · Network Security · Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) · Ubuntu · Internet Protocol Suite (TCP/IP) · Distributed Systems · Rust (Programming Language) · GitHub · Wireshark · REST APIs · User Datagram Protocol (UDP)

positions.description: Led recitations for Religion and Politics in American History course taught by Prof. Heather Curtis at MCI Shirley through the Tufts University Prison Initiative of the Tisch College of Civic Life (TUPIT)

company.name: Jonathan M. Tisch College of Civic Life

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description: Worked on a team of developers building a web app for a local nonprofit
positions.insights: Skills: Node.js · Git · Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) · JavaScript · GitHub

positions.title: Co-Instructor for Teaching Computer Science (CS 4)
positions.description:
- Taught mandatory course for new TAs in the CS department along with Professor Megan Monroe
- Developed and executed a series of 2.5 hour long lectures on necessary skills to be a TA

positions.title: Teaching Fellow for Intro to Computer Science (CS 11)
positions.description:
- In addition to regular TA duties, maintained course infrastructure and course scheduling in collaboration with professor
- Created office hours and lab schedule for 35+ TAs
- Led weekly grading meetings to ensure consistency and accuracy in grading, coordinated and led exam review sessions

positions.title: Teaching Assistant for Internet-scale Distributed Systems (CS 117)
positions.description:
- Held office hours to debug TCP- and UDP-based distributed programming projects 
- Graded written and programming assignments aimed at teaching students about concepts and design challenges of the World Wide Web
- Led lecture on the impacts of the Web

positions.title: Teaching Assistant for Intro to Computer Science (CS 11)
positions.description:
- Co-teaught weekly lab for approximately 20 students, covered important topics in C++, gave students hands on coding practice
- Ran office hours 3x/week to help students design and debug programs
- Graded homework and exams
- Created rubrics for homework assignments

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.insights: Skills: Linux · Git · Lua · Network Security · Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) · Ubuntu · Internet Protocol Suite (TCP/IP) · Distributed Systems · Debugging · Rust (Programming Language) · Programming · Debian · GitHub · Wireshark · User Datagram Protocol (UDP)

positions.title: Teaching Assistant for Pre-College Coding Academy
positions.description:
- Led small group workshops on functions and classes in Python, effective code design, and documentation
- Supported students with varying levels of experience to create final projects using Python

positions.title: Intern
positions.description:
Office of Fmr. Senate Majority Leader Charles E. Schumer 

- Answered phone/voicemails and took note of constituent concerns
- Made phone calls to constituents
- Attended press conferences and roundtables with Sen. Schumer
- Created clippings from newspapers for Sen. Schumer to read
- Conducted research on local organizations
- Prepared regular updates on local politics 
- Created policy guides on Sen. Schumer's positions and actions for myself and other interns

positions.title: Field Intern
positions.locationName: Manhattan, New York, United States (Congressional District NY-12) · On-site
positions.description:
Worked on Rep. Jerry Nadler's successful 2022 Congressional primary against Rep. Carolyn Maloney, Suraj Patel, and Ashmi Sheth. This race was the first time that two Congressional Committee Chairs faced each other in a primary.

- Made phone calls to likely voters to inform them about the election and Rep. Nadler
- Recruited, mobilized, coordinated, and trained volunteers 
- Handed out lit in NYC at greenmarkets, subway stations, and other high traffic locations
- Attended public events with Rep. Nadler
- Dropped literature in apartment complexes
positions.insights: Skills: Canvassing · Political Campaigns · NGP VAN · Phone Banking · Political Organizing
